name: Common frog
note: The common frog (docs 11, 12, 23). The recipe has two halves. The LOOK is body, bake and preview: what a later creature studio, and a player's look layer, may change. The LIFE is ecology, presence and find: needs, numbers, arrival and trust, which no look layer ever touches, so the core loop and catch-up stay the same. LOOK. body: the blended-SDF frog from Matt's pond tier 1 prototype (frog recipe v2), in real meters, body-local +z forward, origin on the ground under the body. prims are blended in order with a smooth minimum of radius k (m); rot is degrees about x, y, z; a capsule's r is [radius at a, radius at b]; a roundCone's scale stretches it about a. The throat sac is at rest (blend kRest). Eyes (Matt, 2026-10-19, after a photo of a frog's face): each eye is hooded from behind and above by a lid of skin (a piece with a part name, lid.l and lid.r, on the head bone; stiff, so its skin follows the head alone and the eye can sink under it). eyeLook: the eye looks out along axis (outward, up, forward), a wide horizontal pupil (half-widths across and up, shares of the radius) in a gold iris (albedo eyeRing) flecked darker (fleck, flecksPerM, fleckShare), beyond irisCos the ball (eye). displayScale: how much larger than life the frog is drawn (Matt, 2026-10-18: 1.5, so frogs read from a little way off on a big screen and show more detail on a phone; 2026-10-21: 2.5, about 20 cm, so players can find them: creatures are the heart of the game); hops, swim float and tongue reach scale with it, and the pad seat numbers (minRadiusM, footM, clearM, dipM, maxOn) are set for the drawn frog, comfort rings stay at real size. shape (S6b): named proportions the frog rig (src/world/creatures/rigs/frog.js) applies to the prims, 1 for the body as drawn here: torso length, width and height (the limbs and head move with the torso), head size (the eyes and throat follow), eye size, throat sac size, hind leg thickness. variation: each of variants seeded body variants nudges every proportion by up to this share and moves the blotches; every frog wears one variant, picked by its id, and is drawn up to sizeJitter larger or smaller. eyeGlint: the wet eyes, a smooth cornea (roughness) that shows a sharp point of sun or moon and the sky at a glancing view, strength times (physically lit; the skin that follows the eye bones). skin: how far (m) past the nearest piece a point of the skin still follows another piece's bone (smaller is a sharper fold at the joints). bake: the cell size (m) the body is meshed at by surface nets (the size preview), and lods: the levels of detail, each a cell size, used out to toM meters from the eye (the last beyond). motion (S6b): breath, the throat sac swelling by sac (share of its size) and the body by torso, hz times a second; blink, every everyS seconds (seeded), lasting s seconds: as a frog does, the eyes sink retractM into the head under their lids, flattened to squash of their height. S6b-2, from Matt's prototype export: frogs move on stepHz steps a second of real time (a hop takes as long at 4x), seeded per frog. hop: distM and heightM real meters (times displayScale, so hops scale with the drawn frog), lasting s seconds (longer for longer hops); the hind legs reach out to reach of their length in flight (two-bone IK) and the forelegs lift by lift (radians). squash: the body's landing spring, amount at most, stiffness k and damping d. call: while calling, a frog calls about perS times a second but waits if any frog started within gapS seconds, so the chorus runs around the pond; each call swells the throat sac to 1 + inflate times its size over pulseS seconds on a spring (k, d); a calling bout lasts boutS seconds. tongue: a flick lasting s seconds reaching reachM (times readability and displayScale) out of the mouth (body point), radiusM thick, albedo linear; while foraging, every everyS seconds. swim: a frog kick every kickS seconds at speedMps (times displayScale), then an eyes-up float of floatS seconds with eyesUpM of the head above the surface; only in water up to maxDepthM deep, where lilies do not grow. forage: a short hop every everyS seconds, then flicks tongue flicks. rest: a small shuffle every shuffleEveryS seconds. leashM: how far from its home on the bank a frog wanders. spacing: a hop never lands within hopBodies body lengths of another frog or its landing, and frogs closer than driftBodies drift apart at driftMps. pads (S6b-3): a frog whose home has lilies near spends about share of its outings on a lily pad, sitting or calling; only on a pad at least minRadiusM across its half (a grown pad), at seatShare of its radius out from the middle opposite the notch, its feet footM from the rim, clear by clearM of any pad that could swing over the seat; a pad within a hop it hops onto; one further out, up to seekM away, it swims to and climbs on from edgeM off its rim; one frog a pad, at most maxOn frogs on pads (the pad drawing dips those pads by dipM under the frog); a swimming frog ducks submergeM under a pad rather than through it, and floats only in open water. dayHide: by day (outside the activity hours, before calling) a frog sits tucked into cover within reachM of home, among the stems, and comes out to the edge at dusk: the cover score of a spot is the best of each kind there (reeds, rushes, iris, and the stool at a grey willow's foot as clumps or per-square cover, grass per square; weighted by cover), a spot counts from minScore, a meter farther off costs perM, searched on a stepM grid, on land or in water up to maxDepthM; it hops there until within atM, and looks again every againS seconds as cover grows; with no cover near, it rests at the edge. clumps: at night a frog sits outside this share of a reed or iris clump's radius, at its edge, never in its stems. moods: share of active time spent swimming; frogs at mood callFromMood or more call, from callAfterDuskH[0] to [1] hours after dusk. preview: the sizes the ?frogscale preview offers (times real), the camera distances (m) and pitches (degrees) of its views. LIFE. ecology (S6a, the hourly tick): dormancy names the window in recipes/world/seasons.json (asleep in the pond mud); activity: crepuscular, hours of the day it is out ([from, to), to past 24 wraps), for S6b. needs: five, each 0..1, mood = their weighted geometric mean (weights w sum to 1). water: distance to good water (still fresh water depthM deep, or a damp hollow), full within okM, none beyond maxM. food: the midge field (recipes/species/midge.json) summed over a square of radiusM around the spot, against perFrog times the group (shares of a full square meter of midges a frog needs). shelter: the best cover within radiusM, each plant weighted (cover), counting from 'from' and full at 'full' (grass alone is no shelter, so a bare grassy bank holds no frogs; long grass with other cover counts toward the web). quiet: what disturbs it by night and day (lanterns and paths, none in the slice, so 1 for now). company: frogs within reachM, full from n[0] to n[2] with n[1] ideal, a lone frog scores alone, a crowd past n[2] falls toward crowded. edge: a bank square beside a pond (still water of at least minPondM2 square meters; a spring's little pool is water, not a shore) is good edge when its score (mood at the ideal group size) is at least goodScore; the island holds one frog per metresPerFrog of good edge. scored: squares scored at all are land or shallows to shallowCm. arrival (times in game hours): the pond is right once the best edge scores rightScore and holds one frog, for rightHoldH hours in a row; a scout may come at dusk (duskOffsetH after sunset) once it has been right scoutAfterH hours and frogs are awake, with scoutChance each dusk and surely by the maxWaitDusks-th; after settleAfterH the scout stays if its mood is settleMood or more (and a second frog comes at the next dusk), else it moves on and none tries again for rescoutAfterH; then at dusk, if a day has passed since the last, mood is joinMood or more and there is room, another comes with joinChance; mood eases moodEase of the way to its target each hour; a frog whose mood stays under leaveMood for leaveAfterH hours, or one too many for the edge, moves on, at most one every leaveEveryH hours; the frogs are happy after happyHoldH hours at mean mood happyMood with happyMin or more. homeApartM: two frogs' homes at least this far apart. gift: what happy frogs give, once (src/world/expansion.js): the Cliff tool, Sculpt's Terrace and Cut (docs 12, 13). presence (doc 23, S6b and S6c; rings in real meters): comfort ring ringM shrinking by ringTrustShrink x trust to ringMinM; a presence source (the camera's eye) inside the ring moving faster than calmSpeed m/s (times 1 + calmTrustGain x trust), or an edit within editReachM, startles a frog: it plops into the water, dives and swims about fleeM away from the source at fleeMps and floats eyes-up, wary for wariS seconds; frogs within hushReachM hush for hushS seconds; quiet watching (trust per minute in stretches of minS to capS within reachM), trust per feeding, the ceiling word and namingTrust. find: a frog is found (its page inks) when you tap the ground within tapM of it, plus tapPerM per meter the camera is away (a frog far off is small on screen), or watch it: keep it within lookM of the middle of your view, zoomed in to lookDistM or closer, for holdS seconds. The close-up limit (35 cm) lives in recipes/world/camera.json.

presence._pace: P2h (October 26, 2026): friendship slowed to about 7 played days to Familiar without treats, about 5 with a treat a day (was about 2), for the trust lab's keeper (tools/trust-lab.html). treatFeeds: a liked treat is worth that many meals (feedTrust), once a game day.
presence._trust: Trust (S6c, doc 23): 0..1 per frog, saved, only ever grows. bands: where each word after Wary begins (Tolerant, Curious, Familiar, Bonded); the ceiling word caps it just under the next band. Quiet watching: the camera slower than watch.stillMps within watch.reachM of a frog for at least watch.minS, closed when it moves or at watch.capS, earns trustPerMin a minute. Both kinds are saved as events the hourly tick applies.
presence._portrait: A Familiar frog (S6c-3) holds still, resting, while a calm source is within portraitM, for portraitHoldS after the last such look: ready for photo mode in M2.

_treat: The frogs' treat (P2h, docs/future/13 section 8; recipes/world/treats.json): cast kelp or wrack from the strandline, set out on land near the pond; the nearest frog within reachM (not one leaving) comes and snaps it up at once, once you are outside its comfort ring, as with food; if that frog swims off, the next one near comes instead, for up to feed.treatLingerS real seconds. id names it in the trust event, the journal's likes:<id> trigger and the treat:taken event.
_feed: Feeding (S6c-2): the Feed tool's food for this species (the tool card's words are in src/ui/tools.js FEED_SPECIES). A frog within reachM of where the food lands (not one leaving) comes for it, once the camera is outside its comfort ring, after waitS, more (up to fullWaitS) if it ate within fullH game hours; food nobody takes is gone after lingerS (real seconds). A meal earns presence.feedTrust, scaled down if it ate within fullH. specks: how many little dark bits, each speckM long, within spreadM; ringM: the soft ring on the ground where food lies. messages: what the card says after a tap.

messages.waiting: A frog has seen it, but waits for you to back off.
messages.none: No frog is near enough to see it. Try closer to one.
messages.water: Frogs take their food on the bank. Try the edge, by a frog.
messages.asleep: The frogs are asleep in the pond mud for winter.
messages.unknown: Nothing here takes food from you yet.

_reveal: Coming back in the reveal on return (S7c, src/world/creatures/reveal-return.js): return is how (plop: a ring on the water, for the few nearest the camera); growS is how long one takes to come in.

voice.note: The frog's voice (doc 17 'pulse-croak', doc 25 'Creature voices'; src/audio/voices.js).json as its voice field at merge (docs/audio-future-work.md). The common frog's call is a soft, low, purring croak, not a bullfrog, so this is gentle and slightly grainy. SOUND: a band-limited pulse train (harmonics partials, each k^-tilt, so it stays soft) repeating at a rate in rateHz (18 to 40 Hz) around baseRateHz, through two resonant bandpass formants (hz, q, db; near 600 Hz and 1.4 kHz) and a soft lowpass at lowpassHz; a little breath noise (breathDb) goes through the same formants. grain shakes each pulse's level (depth, from noise lowpassed at hz) and jitter wobbles its timing (cents, at hz), which is what makes it purr rather than buzz. PHRASE: each call is groups pulse groups (2 to 6, picked per call), each groupS long with gapS between, the pulse rate rising by rateRise across a group; attackS and releaseS round each group; groupAmp is the level of the first, second and later groups, so a phrase leans in and falls away. onsetS is the delay from the call start to the first pulse; the call start is when the game starts swelling the throat sac (recipes/species/frog.json motion.call.pulseS, 0.32 s), so the first group peaks while the sac is full. LEVEL: levelDb at intensity 1, intensityDb from intensity 0 to 1. INDIVIDUAL: each frog (its id hashed with the world seed) keeps a pitch offset within pitch (0.15 = plus or minus 15 percent, moving the formants and a little of the pulse rate) and a rhythm within rhythm (0.2 = plus or minus 20 percent, faster pulses and shorter groups together). SEASONS (doc 25): rate is the call density factor the behaviour applies (spring 1.3, summer 1, autumn 0.5, winter 0, silent); pitch multiplies the formants (autumn 5 percent lower); phrase multiplies how many groups (autumn shorter). The spring purr is a quiet low layer of distant callers under the chorus: a slow pulse train lowpassed at lowpassHz through a band at bandHz, two of them spread left and right (widthCents apart), at db when calls arrive at activityCallsPerS, rising and falling with recent calls over attackS and releaseS, and only in spring (by the spring weight). SPATIAL (doc 17): each call is its own placed voice, inverse distance from refDistance 2 m, rolloff 1, an air-absorption lowpass from 18 kHz at 2 m to 3 kHz at 60 m. maxVoices: at most this many calls sound at once, nearest first (a far call is dropped, or the farthest stopped, when full).
